newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai exchange calls for company improvements.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai exchange calls for company improvements.

text.p: The Shanghai Stock Exchange on Saturday called on listed companies to improve disclosure of information and to provide special training for company secretaries.

In an article in the Shanghai Securities News, the exchange's deputy director, Wu Yalun, said the exchange was determined to strengthen supervision of listed companies in spite of the rapid growth in numbers.
More than a third of the 300 or so companies now listed on the Shanghai exchange have been added in the past year.
"We must raise the level of transparency of information disclosure and make it more standardised," he said. "We must also improve the training of company secretaries."
In June, the exchange issued regulations requiring all listed companies to employ a company secretary responsible for releasing information and contacts with the exchange and other officials.
Wu said all company secretaries must attend a training course of 5-7 days and take an examination on its completion.
